root_idea.summary: The supplied evidence centers on the spider, understood as the web-weaving insect, with related formations naming associated creatures and descriptive compounds.
root_idea.development: No independent Maqāyīs or other root-development discussion was supplied; the broader semantic development is therefore stated cautiously from the lexical evidence.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested noun is presented under its normalized classical citation form.

senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic possessive construction بَيْتُ العَنْكَبُوتِ, the noun refers to the spider whose house or web is mentioned; this is a constructional use of the same noun, not a separate basic noun sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A short person; as an epithet, a term associated with blackness and shortness, and possibly used synonymously with عَنْكَبُوتٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence reports both the sense “short” and an alternative epithet use related to the spider term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A worm or maggot engendered in a honeycomb and spoiling the honey.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct Classical Arabic specialization of the same headword, not attested in the supplied Quranic occurrences.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A he-goat whose horn is curved so as to resemble a ring.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional descriptive compound referring to the shape of the horn.
